# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (for later lookup; not commentary)

## BOOK 1 of 2: "The Princess of the Atom" by Ray Cummings (Gutenberg #75690; Avon reprint 1950; orig. 1929 Munsey)
Dedication: to "my son, Hal, and to Russ, my son-in-law--both chemists."
Blurb: Giants off New England coast the day Dianne returns; Dr. Ferrule's ward; Frank Ferrule, Drake Ferrule, Togaro ("lustful," "would rule the universe"); "Atomic Napoleon." Edited by Donald A. Wollheim (AVON FANTASY NOVELS series).

Table of contents (32 chapter titles, plus Prologue): The Coming of the Giants; The Mysterious Visitor; The Signal Fire; The Strange Island; Princess of the Atom; The Chase into Smallness; The Flight in the Cellular Caverns; Death of the Giants; Tiny Fragment of Rock; The White Flag; Giant in Ambush; The Meeting; The Stowaway; The Locked Door; Togaro at Bay; Frank's Plan; The Tiny Prowler; The Escape of Togaro; Night of Turmoil; In the Blood Light of Dawn; Riding the Giant; "Vengeance of Togaro!"; Doomed Little Planet!; The End of a World; In the Campfire Light; The Black and White Flags; The Fight on the Rock Summit; The Return to Earth; The Theft of the Rock; The World at Bay; Togaro Strikes; The Fugitives; The Combat of Titans; Princess of the Cottage.
Epigraph: "Beautiful with a grace beyond the reach of art."

**Prologue**: Narrator Frank Ferrule (17). Father: consulting chemist, slender, ~50, iron-gray hair, horn-rimmed spectacles. Brother Drake (6'2", six years older, blond, good-natured; "huge dog"). Frank called "terrier," small, dark-haired. Sister Dianne (younger than Drake, Frank's favorite; flaxen/golden hair, blue eyes, exquisite beauty; hair grows in a low peak on forehead, parted to side; hides a silver crescent-shaped scar on forehead). Mother died when Frank a child. Family summer home on Maine coast, King's Cove, near town of Elton. Bird's Nest Island: tiny rocky island ~2 miles offshore, fifty-foot central rock peak, spring of water, signal fire/flag childhood game.
- August 14 (five years before giants): Dianne (16) vanishes on island while swimming; clothes left on beach. Frank had tugged her hair in water ("You hurt me"). Drake and Frank searched.
- Father reveals: 15 years earlier, he and wife (mother) found infant girl (about 1 yr old) on Bird's Nest Island in thicket; wearing golden gossamer long-sleeved robe with tiny hood (kept in father's desk drawer); silver crescent-shaped mark on forehead. Named Dianne by mother. Father taught her to hide the mark.
- Father once said: "wondered if she were just exactly human like the rest of us."

**Chapter I – Coming of the Giants**: March 20, first giant seen by small steamship (out of Halifax, bound Portland) near Cape Sable, Nova Scotia; stood waist-deep, ~60 ft visible above water (estimated). Later reports at Penobscot River mouth, near Bay of Fundy; late March. Frank is a pilot for International Mail Service (Boston–St. John). Night patrol flight with relief pilot Bob Jones and radioman Green (code radio), Frank senior pilot; plane leaves Boston ~10 pm. Giant at cove near King's Cove; kills two people on cliff with swing of arm. Giant swims toward Bird's Nest Island, dives, vanishes. Message from father: "He has heard from Dianne." Land at Bennett Field, NY. Father's chief: Ferrule; Frank's chief ref.

**Chapter II – Mysterious Visitor**: Westchester home (father and Drake, lab in NYC). ~midnight, man thumps on door; tall, bulky, long dark overcoat, black felt hat, foreign accent, heavy-jawed, hairless, ~35. Bullet head, pale gold close-cut hair, slate-blue eyes, high-bridged nose, square chin. Says "You had a daughter--" "I came to warn you," "Stay away from... Maine," "giants... dangerous," "You will never see Dianne again. Forget her." Hat worn backward; stoops at door; sits awkwardly like never having seen chair. Leaves running. (Later identified as Togaro.)

**Chapter III – Signal Fire**: Frank arrives morning. Father: "one of the giants." They return to Maine by official plane; stay at King's Cove house under military rule; Elton half-deserted; officer knows father. Father has automatic; rifles. Night vigil. Morning: smoke signal from Bird's Nest Island — two large puffs, three smaller = childhood signal.

**Chapter IV – Strange Island**: Frank, Drake row to island with rifle, automatics, oilskins. Campfire embers wet. Tiny figures in grass; Dianne emerges, finger-sized; calls "Frank... Dianne, it's you!"

**Chapter V – Princess of the Atom**: Dianne grows to normal size with companion Ahlma (golden hair, paler crescent, robe pale silvery white; her servant and friend; accent like Togaro's). Dianne's home: infinitely small world in an atom of meteorite on island; Togaro (leader) took her into smallness 5 years ago; rescued by people; now ruler. Togaro learned English from her. Togaro's giants (6 at island, storm). Mission: get the rock fragment (atom's crater), guard it. Father hides in room; rug at door; lamp. Togaro (tiny man in corner) spotted; Drake throws chair; Dianne asks Frank & Drake to follow Togaro into smallness.

**Chapter VI – The Chase into Smallness**: Pellets in phial at Dianne's waist (sweetish taste). Shrinking in bedroom; cellular caverns (wood structure). Togaro lures them; giant-sized fights Drake (Drake gulped whole pellet) in cavern; Drake and Togaro fight through roof opening. Frank wants more drug; denied.

**Chapter VII – Flight in Cellular Caverns**: Father & Ahlma watch; Ahlma says "I see--One of them!"; Drake (tiny) fights Togaro, who grows; Togaro flings lamp? (Ahlma flings lamp), Togaro grabs father, runs out.

**Chapter VIII – Death of the Giants**: Afternoon; Drake bruised. Night to island with Dianne & Ahlma; signal fire embers; meteorite projection (copper, pitted, metallic), crater on top. Storm; six giants on island; dory crushed; war planes, battleship (Canadian/US forces). Giants die; one reaches mainland 10 miles down coast. Dianne says Frank must chip off fragment after they leave; Drake dwindles away with girls. Frank chips off fragment (chunk few inches) and is found by men.

**Chapter IX – Tiny Fragment of Rock**: A year later; fragment kept in barred room with guards. May: tiny man appears with white flag.

**Chapter X – White Flag**: Room sealed (Kings Cove). Guard Foley; Ransome (second guard). Man: "Alt," says "Don't kill me. Friend from Drake." Alt says Drake, Dianne, Ahlma in flying car waiting; wants weapons (knife, automatics). Frank agrees to go in.

**Chapter XI – Giant in Ambush**: Frank wears bathing suit, drug belt (8 compartments each side; two drugs opposite action), four automatics, knives. Alt's feet bandaged. Frank shrinks; father lifts them with hand; giant ambush in valley (Togaro man). Frank fires twice.

**Chapter XII – The Meeting**: Escape into cleft, crescent pit, descent; tiny figure climbs Frank's belt (Togaro, unnoticed). Long journey, mountain tunnels, metallic plain, rain. Meet Drake (red signal light) near forest; Dianne kisses Frank.

**Chapter XIII – The Stowaway**: Flying car: elongated globe, 40 ft, woven metal wire hull. Drake explains Togaro's Mita-based plan (half-million followers; conquer earth). Togaro (small) steals automatic; escapes.

**Chapter XIV – Locked Door**: Voyage through molecules, space, stars. Guard murdered (bodkin in chest) in passage. Girls' stateroom locked.

**Chapter XV – Togaro at Bay**: Ahlma unconscious; Dianne taken by Togaro. Togaro in another cabin laughs: "Come in and get us--if you dare!"

**Chapter XVI – Frank's Plan**: Togaro holds Dianne in lap, threatens with enlarging drug. Frank's plan: secretly shrink, sneak in while Drake covers.

**Chapter XVII – Tiny Prowler**: Frank tiny; climbs Togaro's trousers; grabs Togaro's belt strap.

**Chapter XVIII – Escape of Togaro**: Togaro takes enlarging drug; ceiling breaks; he leaps out to Mita's landing field, carrying Dianne. Frank clinging to belt. Mita description: planet ~300 miles diameter, six-hour-forty-minute rotation, moon, sun ~20 million miles off; capital "Shore City" on lake; Dianne's palace.

**Chapter XIX – Night of Turmoil**: Drake & Ahlma & Alt; Jain (official, huge black-coated). Palace on hill with lake view.

**Chapter XX – In the Blood Light of Dawn**: Mob "The world ends tonight! Give us the drugs!" Togarite giants rise, carrying tiny followers; exodus to island ship; Togaro's vehicle expands; Drake & Ahlma & Alt shrink to top of spire.

**Chapter XXI – Riding the Giant**: Frank on Togaro's belt; Dianne on his neck; to island encampment; Frank ropes down through window.

**Chapter XXII – "Vengeance of Togaro!"**: Frank reaches Dianne in cabin; Togaro: "Vengeance of Togaro! Ten million people die, because Togaro is angry!" Togaro plans to drag Mita into sun.

**Chapter XXIII – Doomed Little Planet!**: Mita hurled by Togaro toward its sun; falls.

**Chapter XXIV – End of a World**: Drake organizes escape; ~110,000 refugees taken; Mita falls into sun.

**Chapter XXV – In the Campfire Light**: Togarite camp on Earth-side forest; Frank steals jacket and hat; Dianne at camp; Frank fights Togaro with rock; Togaro's knock-out.

**Chapter XXVI – Black and White Flags**: Frank and Dianne escape upward; black-and-white flag signal; reunion with Drake, Ahlma, Alt. Discovery: rock stolen.

**Chapter XXVII – Fight on the Rock Summit**: Four Togarite guards; Alt wounded (bar in side); Frank hits; Drake shoots one.

**Chapter XXVIII – Return to Earth**: Escape from room; into King's Cove boathouse, night; Togarite camp outside.

**Chapter XXIX – Theft of the Rock**: Explanation: Togaro escaped with Alt; Foley killed; father knocked unconscious; rock stolen (May 14-15). May 20-21 giants at King's Cove.

**Chapter XXX – World at Bay**: Giants occupy Maine towns (Elton etc.); Portland occupied May 23; Lynn destroyed; battleship sunk by Togaro; Canadian planes shot down by slings.

**Chapter XXXI – Togaro Strikes**: War Secretary; giants reach Long Island Sound, New Haven June 1, Bear Mountain Bridge torn loose. Togaro at Sandy Hook June 2; wrecks Staten Island forts, Lower Manhattan; demands US yield. Drake's message: "Don't yield! We're coming with the drugs." Attack ordered; Dianne-figure giant.

**Chapter XXXII – Fugitives**: Frank, Dianne, Drake, Ahlma flee; Dianne runs (drug). Frank pursues.

**Chapter XXXIII – Combat of Titans**: Dianne and Frank grow >500 ft; Togaro swims to Long Island; Dianne fights Togaro; Togaro takes poison; he flings the rock globe into sea (fragment destroyed). Togaro falls in Lower Bay.

**Chapter XXXIV – Princess of the Cottage**: One year later; giants' followers isolated on an island; Togaro's body sunk; drugs destroyed. Frank & Dianne living in cottage; Drake & Ahlma nearby; father in New York. Dianne: "Frank Ferrule, you can make your own smoke signals for Drake and Ahlma. I'm going to bed."

Back-cover blurb lines: "Giants rise up out of the sea"; "Atomic Napoleon"; "invasion of America by an army of giants tall as the Empire State Building"; "destruction of a planet by one man's wrath."

## BOOK 2 of 2: "The Boys of Grand Pré School" by Prof. James De Mille (Gutenberg #56232; "B. O. W. C." series; Boston: Lee & Shepard; illustrated)
Setting: Grand Pré Academy, Nova Scotia (Minas Basin, Blomidon, Cornwallis, Gaspereaux River, Horton Bluff, Mud Creek, North Mountain, Scott's Bay, Hall's Harbor, Cape Split, Ile Haute, Pereau, Annapolis/Port Royal, Louisbourg, Halifax).

Key characters:
- **Bart** (Bart Rawdon? leader; imaginative, improvises rhymes; "Brethren of the B.O.W.C."). Brothers **Bruce** and **Arthur** Rawdon (Bruce tall, superstitious, courageous). **Phil**, **Tom**. **Pat** (Irish, prankster; owns the garret/ghost trick, owl). **Solomon** (Black cook, "Grand Panjandrum," says "Dinna"; "Bee See Double Bubble" society). **Captain Corbet** (old sea captain, schooner *Antelope*, baby son, wife "Mrs. Corbet"; mineral rod). **Mr. Long** (teacher, eloquent). **Mr. Simmons** (teacher). **Dr. Porter** (headmaster, antiquarian). **Captain Pratt** (jovial, salvages Antelope). **Jiggins, Bogud (David Digg), Billymack, Johnny Blue, Muckle, Sammy Ram Ram** (other boys). **Pieter Schwab** (justice of the peace). **Old Zeke** (witness, drunk). **Bennie Grigg** and Mrs. Grigg (Scott's Bay). **Smalley**, **Atkins**, **Slocum** (owl's owner). **Gaspereaugians** (rival valley boys).

Plot in order:
I. Spring recess last day; B.O.W.C. camp in woods; Solomon's lunch; they make bows, arrows, whistles. Captain Corbet appears; "mineral rod" (a stick); copper coin "LOUIS XIV. ROI DE FRANCE"; finds pot of gold in "Old French Orchard" cellar; silver/money of Benedict Bellefontaine.
II. Old French Orchard, Acadian history (Evangeline); cellar; rod drops at center. Plan: dig at midnight.
III. Midnight dig with lanterns, Solomon as watcher, incantations (Phil: English history; Tom: Euclid; Arthur: Arnold's Latin; Bruce: Latin; Bart: Caesar); hymn to "Rousseau's Dream." Iron metal struck; terrifying roar; panic and flight; Bruce returns; they fill hole.
IV. Mr. Long asks boys to unload ballast stones from Antelope to rebuild wall, for holidays. Antelope capsizes in Mud Creek, Corbet's "gone sucker" speech.
   Captain Corbet is sued by prosecutor (potato field owner) for wall damages ($500).
V. Mysterious noises in attic/garret; Bart explores; Pat suspected.
VI. Trial before Pieter Schwab; Old Zeke's rat; Mr. Long's oration about the "babby"; case dismissed.
VII. Gaspereaux Valley expedition; fishing; Gaspereaugians absent; ambush at camp.
VIII. Bart and Solomon captured by Gaspereaugians; Bruce wrestles big Gaspereaugian (throws him in pool); prisoners escape with basket.
IX. Donkey's bray revealed as cause of roar (donkey belonged to Dr. Porter; bought from "ole scissa grinda"). Second dig: a plowshare, colter, bolts, chain, iron pot, copper sous ("UN SOU"), bone.
X. Dr. Porter laughing; relics given to museum.
XII. Blomidon expedition, North Mountain breakfast; Dr. Porter's Acadian history lecture (Louisbourg, Acadian expulsion).
XIII–XVI. Woods wanderings; Dr. Porter loses way; surf at cliff; Pat chases porcupine; party splits; Bruce's group wanders in circles; reunite near Scott's Bay (Bennie Grigg's house, fish smell).
XVII. Bennie's feast; Sunday services; return Monday; extra holiday.
XVIII. Garret mystery resolved: Pat rang bell by string; owl (Slocum's escaped screech owl) caused howls; donkey hauled up to garret.
XIX. Donkey bray scares Pat.
XX. Confession; Solomon insults owl; school discipline (Mr. Long).
XXI. Captain Corbet brings baby to Mr. Long, who leaves; relics displayed with plowshare speech and Bart's poem "True Theory of the Bone" (bone of "Parley Yoo," leg shot).
XXII. Doctor's lectures on Acadians and Louisbourg (Pepperell expedition 1745).
XXIII–XXIV. Antelope raised by Captain Pratt; Pat babysits baby; Corbet departs with potatoes to Boston; sails into fog bank.
